html:
Santeria, or Regla de Ocha, is a religion that grew in Cuba among enslaved Yoruba people from West Africa, brought in great numbers during the sugar boom of the 1800s. It honours spirits called orishas, often linked with Catholic saints.

Followers serve the orishas with drumming, song, dance and offerings, guided by priests and the divination system of Ifa. Black mutual aid societies called cabildos kept the faith alive under slavery.

Santeria was long hidden or persecuted, including in the first decades after the revolution. Today it is open and widespread in Cuba and has spread with the Cuban diaspora to Miami, New York and beyond. It is a cousin of Haitian Vodou and of Candomble in Brazil.
